title: Revision bug: Lambda' deletes nonzero off-diagonal cells (a,b,b,b); eq:roffeqLam false

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**NEW gap (revision-introduced): deleting degenerate columns discards nonzero off-diagonal data; `eq:roffeqLam` is false.**

The current `solution.tex` revises the earlier wrong invariant (issues q9-8/q9-9) by passing, in Thm `lower` Step A, to the matrix $\Lambda'^{(m)}\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n^3-n)}$ obtained by deleting **every** column whose triple $(\beta,\gamma,\delta)$ is *degenerate* ($\beta=\gamma=\delta$). But a degenerate column $(\beta,\beta,\beta)$ at row $\alpha\ne\beta$ is the cell $(\alpha,\beta,\beta,\beta)$, which is **off-diagonal and nonzero**. So $\Lambda'^{(m)}$ throws away $n(n-1)$ genuine off-diagonal cells ($20$ per mode at $n=5$).

Consequently the claimed equivalence
$$\text{eq:roffeqLam}:\quad r_m^{\mathrm{off}}\le1\iff \operatorname{rank}\Lambda'^{(m)}\le1$$
is **FALSE in the $\Leftarrow$ direction**, where $r_m^{\mathrm{off}}=\min_{\widehat\lambda}\operatorname{rank}\widehat\lambda_{(m)}$ is the min mode-$m$ rank over diagonal completions of the *full* off-diagonal data (as Thm `extract` defines it).

**Explicit counterexample (verified numerically, $n=5$, mode $1$).** Choose the ordinary-column part rank-one, $\lambda_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}=\xi_\alpha\eta_{\beta\gamma\delta}$ for ordinary $(\beta,\gamma,\delta)$, and assign **arbitrary nonzero** values to the cells $(\alpha,\beta,\beta,\beta)$, $\alpha\ne\beta$. Then:
- $\operatorname{rank}\Lambda'^{(1)}=1$ (ordinary columns only), but
- a $2\times2$ minor mixing an ordinary column with a degenerate-column cell is nonzero ($\approx 2.71$), so **no rank-$1$ completion of the full mode-$1$ off-diagonal exists**: $r_1^{\mathrm{off}}=5$.

Hence $\Lambda'$ is **not** "the fully-observed off-diagonal data with no missing entries"; the classical "rank $\le1$ $\iff$ all $2\times2$ minors vanish" argument in `solution.tex` is applied to the wrong matrix. This invalidates `eq:roffeqLam` and the way it is used in Thm `lower` Step A and Lemma `offrank1` (eq:Lamrank1).

NOTE: this is distinct from q9-8/q9-9. q9-9 proposed exactly this fix ($\rho^{\ne}_m$ = delete all-equal column triples); **this issue shows that proposed fix is itself incorrect** (see also the companion issue on the false rank law).

**Suggested repair.** Treat as *free* only the $n$ all-equal **cells** $(a,a,a,a)$ (one per row, all in distinct columns), NOT entire degenerate columns. With that definition $r_m^{\mathrm{off}}\le1$ is the honest "all off-diagonal $2\times2$ minors vanish, no zero row" statement and the all-equal free cells can always be completed to preserve rank $\le1$.
